paper.title_en: Optical Discovery of New and Candidate Galactic Supernova Remnants Plus Optical Imaging of the Monogem Ring Supernova Remnant
paper.abstract_en: We report the discovery of new and candidate Galactic supernova remnants made through over 1500 hours of H$α$ and [O III] imaging using amateur class instrumentation. These nebulae range from 1 to over 8 degrees in size. Five of these, namely G27.8-17.1, G115.6+9.2, G190.5+25.3, G195.9+2.2 and G239.9+7.0 exhibit low-dispersion optical spectra indicating shock emission by the presence of strong [S II] $λλ$6716,6731 and [O I] $λ$6300 line emissions relative to H$α$, or exhibit a nonradiative shock generated Balmer dominated spectrum. Their filamentary emission morphology also supports the presence of interstellar shock fronts. Two other optical nebulae, G191.3+11.1 and G205.7-1.7, appear likely to be remnants and are proposed as new SNR candidates. We also present [O III] and H$α$ images of optical filaments associated with the 25 degree diameter Monogem Ring SNR which reveal extensive emission-line filaments around most of the remnant's X-ray boundaries. Deep images of the large and [O III] emission dominated SNR G206.6+6.1 seen toward Monogem SNR's center are also included. Key findings of this work include: 1) optical surveys can sometimes detect SNRs especially at high Galactic latitudes and toward the Galactic anti-center direction better than radio and X-ray SNR searches, 2) Balmer nonradiative shocks appear not uncommon in high Galactic latitude SNRs, and 3) faint [O III] emission dominated SNRs may have been missed in H$α$ emission surveys.
